content: 1. Scones are excluded from this category (refer to 2f). Leavened flatbreads such as naan are also excluded (refer to 11c). 2. Flatbreads include all types of leavened and unleavened flatbreads, such as tortillas, wraps, pita, Greek flatbreads, and naan. These may be flavored with salt or other seasonings. Refrigerated and frozen doughs are included, but pancakes are excluded (refer to 2e). 3. Sodium content data for flatbreads is available from four countries (Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka), covering 32 products. The average sodium content is 299 mg/100g, with a median of 274 mg/100g. The 25th percentile is 144 mg/100g, and the 75th percentile is 357 mg/100g. Compliance with the global sodium benchmark is 66%. 4. While two-thirds of flatbread products meet the WHO global sodium benchmark, stricter regional sodium targets have not been established due to limited data. Countries may consider setting lower sodium targets if more than 66% of flatbreads fall below 320 mg/100g. 5. Fish and seafood products, including mollusks, crustaceans, and echinoderms (e.g., sardines, mackerel, shrimp, crab, clams, and smoked oysters), are included in this category. Retort-packed products are included, but canned anchovies are excluded (refer to 14c). 6. Sodium content data for fish and seafood products is available from three countries (Bhutan, India, and Sri Lanka), covering 55 products. The average sodium content is 449 mg/100g, with a median of 340 mg/100g. The 25th percentile is 188 mg/100g, and the 75th percentile is 480 mg/100g. Compliance with the global sodium benchmark is 51%. 7. More than one-third of fish and seafood products already meet the WHO global sodium benchmark. 8. Processed fish and seafood products include raw, unprepared fish and seafood, cakes, burgers, seasoned (with sauce or seasoning), breaded, battered, and stuffed fish. Restructured, simulated, or imitation seafoods such as surimi are also included, as well as fish and seafood-based mousse, spreads, and dips. 9. Sodium content data for processed fish and seafood products is available from four countries (Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, and Sri Lanka), covering 21 products. The average sodium content is 522 mg/100g, with a median of 448 mg/100g. The 25th percentile is 399 mg/100g, and the 75th percentile is 630 mg/100g. Compliance with the global sodium benchmark is 14%. 10. An interim sodium target of 450 mg/100g is recommended to be achieved within four years, followed by further reductions based on compliance reviews. Less than one-third of products currently meet the WHO benchmark. For most non-compliant products, less than a 10% annual reduction is needed to achieve the interim target. 11. Non-heat-treated smoked fish, kippered fish, salmon jerky, anchovies, and dried fish are included in this category. Sodium content data is limited, with an average of 2167 mg/100g and a median of 2251 mg/100g. The 25th percentile is 1248 mg/100g, and the 75th percentile is 3120 mg/100g. Compliance with the global sodium benchmark is 14%. 12. Many products in South-East Asia include pickled fish or seafood and dried fish. Interim targets should be considered despite limited data. 13. Raw meat products and preparations include unprepared meat products, burgers, and fresh sausages. Marinated, flavored, moisture-enhanced, and breaded meat products are also included. 14. Sodium content data for raw meat products is available from three countries (Bangladesh, India, and Sri Lanka), covering 32 products. The average sodium content is 504 mg/100g, with a median of 483 mg/100g. The 25th percentile is 308 mg/100g, and the 75th percentile is 562 mg/100g. Compliance with the global sodium benchmark is 19%. 15. An interim sodium target of 485 mg/100g is recommended to be achieved within four years, followed by further reductions based on compliance reviews. Less than one-third of products currently meet the WHO benchmark. For most non-compliant products, less than a 10% annual reduction is needed to achieve the interim target. 16. Emulsion-based dips, sauces, and dressings include cream or cheese dips, standardized salad dressings (e.g., mayonnaise-based, oil-and-vinegar-based, and creamy dressings), and mayonnaise. Sodium content data is available from three countries (India, Maldives, and Sri Lanka), covering 73 products. The average sodium content is 699 mg/100g, with a median of 669 mg/100g. The 25th percentile is 464 mg/100g, and the 75th percentile is 800 mg/100g. Compliance with the global sodium benchmark is 33%. 17. Soy sauce, fish sauce, and other fermented sauces are included in this category. Sodium content data is available from three countries (India, Indonesia, and Thailand), covering 70 products. The average sodium content is 6929 mg/100g, with a median of 7000 mg/100g. The 25th percentile is 5715 mg/100g, and the 75th percentile is 8117 mg/100g. Compliance with the global sodium benchmark is 16%. 18. An interim sodium target of 6325 mg/100g (33rd percentile) is recommended to be achieved within four years, followed by further reductions based on compliance reviews. The 33rd percentile was chosen to drive substantial sodium reformulation in high-sodium products. 19. Asian-style cooking sauces (e.g., teriyaki, black bean, hoisin, stir-fry, duck, and oyster sauces) are included in this category. Sodium content data is available from three countries (India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand), covering 27 products. The average sodium content is 2848 mg/100g, with a median of 2600 mg/100g. The 25th percentile is 1527 mg/100g, and the 75th percentile is 3970 mg/100g. Compliance with the global sodium benchmark is 4%. 20. An interim sodium target of 2600 mg/100g is recommended to be achieved within four years, followed by further reductions based on compliance reviews. One of 27 products currently meets the WHO benchmark. 21. The interquartile range (25th–75th percentile) was used as a measure of variability to demonstrate the distribution of sodium levels across food categories. Unlike the range, the interquartile range is not affected by extreme values or outliers.
